content: 1. The effect of sonidegib may be altered by its interaction with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, limit its administration to less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse effects. 2. Both sorafenib and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of erythromycin lactobionate and sotalol, which also increases the QTc interval, is contraindicated. 3. Sotorasib decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of sparsentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is needed, but blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function should be regularly monitored if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. St. John’s Wort decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects the metabolism of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor for increased or decreased effects. Stiripentol increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur when co-administered with stiripentol. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of sufentanil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1, which may increase sulbactam plasma concentrations. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Both erythromycin lactobionate and sulfamethoxazole increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of sunitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both sunitinib and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of suvorexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tacrolimus via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both tacrolimus and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tadalafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day or 10 mg every 72 hours for as-needed use. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of talazoparib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tamsulosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 17. Tazemetostat increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per its prescribing information. 18. Tecovirimat decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 19. Both erythromycin lactobionate and telavancin increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effect of temocillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of temsirolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Tepotinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 23. Both erythromycin lactobionate and tetrabenazine increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tezacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of theophylline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the level or effect of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Both erythromycin lactobionate and thioridazine increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tipranavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tobramycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Co-administration of inhaled tobramycin and erythromycin lactobionate increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Monitor closely. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tofacitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but the tofacitinib dose should be decreased if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tolvaptan via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Topiramate decreases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of topotecan via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid co-administration with P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level of toremifene by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of toremifene with agents causing QT prolongation should be avoided. If required, interrupt toremifene therapy or closely monitor the patient with ECGs. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of trabectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of tramadol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction or adjustment of dosing interval may be required. There is an increased risk of serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. Monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of trazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both trazodone and erythromycin lactobionate increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of triazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Both erythromycin lactobionate and trifluoperazine increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Both erythromycin lactobionate and trimethoprim increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 45. Both erythromycin lactobionate and trimipramine increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Trofinetide increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting OATP131 and OATP13B. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Both erythromycin lactobionate and tropisetron increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 49. Tucatinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effect of the live typhoid vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the live bacterial vaccine. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 52. Both erythromycin lactobionate and valbenazine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications in case of potential drug interactions. 54. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level of valproic acid by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the level or effect of valsartan by inhibiting OATP1B1, which may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Both erythromycin lactobionate and vandetanib increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
